title: AI-Authorized Prescription Renewal (Utah Pilot)
content: During the mitigation period, a participant may use its AI technology to authorize the renewal of a verified prescription for a Utah resident and issue such prescriptions to a pharmacist licensed under Utah Code §58-17b. Mitigation applies solely to the renewal workflow described in the Proposal; it does not extend to new prescriptions, other services, or products outside the authorized scope.
pub:source_review_unresolved: The signed source PDF body retains the title DRAFT AGREEMENT although the official OAIP page and filename present it as final and the PDF contains signatures dated October 23-24, 2025.
The May 19, 2026 outcomes report says its limited sample is based on reports from Doctronic physicians and that OAIP initiated a separate independent review.

OAIP's register and FAQ describe a 2026 amendment changing the Phase 2 criteria and removing two medications, which conflicts with the retained signed agreement; no amendment document is linked, so its date, signatories, and exact text are unverified.

No retained source shows an extension request or decision under Section 13, a termination, or compliance; the register's Active status and Phase 1 statement are agency web statements retrieved 2026-09-24.
The register's third-party adversarial testing term and the FAQ's malpractice insurance expectation do not appear in the retained signed agreement text.
The UAC R156-1 link returned HTTP 404 and was removed; no current official Office of Administrative Rules URL was retained.
